# Row S1. After the process that hosts the engine exits, a joined run that still waits has an engine again: status names the engine of the joined command, not "no engine runs".
isolate
! exec bd version
! exec gh version

example review-loop/project.star config/projects/orders.star
exec beehestreal item add orders ui-1 --title 'UI' --body-file body.txt
exec beehestreal item add orders base-1 --title 'Base' --body-file body.txt

exec beehestreal run ui-1 orders --workflow flow/wait.star &ui&
waitstatus 'question of ui-1'
exec beehestreal run base-1 orders --workflow flow/wait.star &base&
waitstatus 'question of base-1'
exec beehestreal answer ui-1 done
wait ui
waitstatus 'engine: run, pid'
exec beehestreal status
stdout 'item-base-1-r1'
! stdout 'no engine runs'
exec beehestreal answer base-1 done
wait base

-- body.txt --
Wait.
-- flow/wait.star --
def main(item):
    wait(name = "close", question = "question of " + item.id)
